svg.title: Why every edge touching a wait is redundant

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: M waits at W12 (M1). L0 left W12, so the rule adds L0 → M1. But M had to ENTER W12 first (M0), and the

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: same rule already gave L0 → M0. Path L0 → M0 → M1 makes the red edge redundant.

g.text: (b) Edge OUT of a wait · Theorem 1

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: N enters W12 later (N2), so the rule adds M1 → N2 (M's wait 'leaves' W12). But M's next move M2 really

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: leaves W12, and gives M2 → N2. Path M1 → M2 → N2 makes the red edge redundant.

g.text: (c) So the waits can go: contract each lane

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: With every type-2 edge on M1 and N1 redundant, delete the two wait vertices and join the neighbours

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: with a type-1 edge. Here M0 → M2 and N0 → N2.

g.text: Only the GRAPH loses the wait. AGV M still stands at W12: if X is slow, M simply

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: does not get the 'go' for M2 yet. The wait now emerges from the dependencies

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: instead of being a 1-step timer, so M can go the moment X2 is done.

g.text: M0 → N1 (M leaves W11, N waits at W11) is the third case; it is replaced by M0 → N0 → N1, exactly as in panel (a). All edges computed by scripts/adg/adg.py.
